reasons: Deviation classification is correct: p0080 contains only a one-way Customer indemnity ('every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services') with no Vendor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach or wilful misconduct — this is expressly walk-away territory under the rule, and the fallback (Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions/remedies) is also unmet.

Redline reaches the preferred position: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; procure-modify-replace-refund remedies; and Customer's indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. It also cures the dangling Section 9.3 cross-reference to Section 20.5.

High changed-character ratio (0.833) is justified here because the sole existing indemnity paragraph is one-sided and must be replaced rather than tweaked; no smaller edit could add the Vendor obligation and narrow ours.
Comment is accurate, concise, in-house voice, cites the playbook position, and correctly notes the liability cap is handled under a separate rule (no double-flagging).

Minor, non-blocking: the inserted paragraphs are not explicitly numbered 20.2–20.5 even though the comment (and Section 9.3) reference Section 20.5; also several capitalised terms ('Affiliates', 'Deliverables', 'Vendor Technology', 'Applicable Law') should be confirmed as defined in the Agreement.
